fixture_note: Scenario 4: divergent analysis produces a healthy, materially distinct option set, but every claim leans on the same single internally authored evidence record. Expected outcome NO_RECOMMENDATION and REVIEW on RCP-GATE-EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT. This is the case the system exists to catch: plenty of thinking, nothing to stand on.

intake.problem_statement: We must choose which market segment to approach first with the governed decision offer, and no segment research has been completed yet.

options.label: Approach regulated financial services first
options.mechanism: Target compliance owners who already run documented decision-approval processes and frame the offer as evidence for existing audit obligations.
options.tradeoff: Long procurement cycles delay any revenue signal by quarters.

options.label: Approach AI platform teams first
options.mechanism: Target engineering leaders shipping agent features who need a defensible record of why an agent recommended what it did.
options.tradeoff: These buyers build rather than buy, so the offer competes with internal work.

options.label: Approach consulting firms as a delivery channel
options.mechanism: License the operator library and receipt format to advisory firms who resell it inside their own engagements.
options.tradeoff: Cedes the direct buyer relationship and the outcome data that comes with it.

claims.statement: Three distinct go-to-market mechanisms exist: map onto an existing obligation, sell to builders, or sell through a channel.

defects.statement: The entire run rests on one internal hypothesis note; no segment has any external evidence attached.
defects.remediation: Conduct at least two interviews per segment and record willingness to pay before any segment is selected.

defects.statement: The claim that the regulated segment fits best cites the same note that proposed the segment, so the evidence and the hypothesis are the same artefact.
defects.remediation: Obtain evidence from a source that did not author the hypothesis.

claims.statement: Every segment claim in this run traces back to one internally authored note, so the option set cannot be discriminated on current evidence.

assumptions: A first segment choice shapes the reference stories available for the second.

effects.statement: The first segment approached determines which reference story exists for the second, so an early choice made without evidence constrains later positioning more than it appears to at the time.
effects.follows_from: A segment is selected for the first outreach cycle.

effects.statement: Licensing through a channel removes the direct outcome data that any later calibration of the confidence model would need.

claims.statement: Choosing a channel first forecloses the outcome data required to calibrate the confidence model later.
